verdict.line: You win if you force short, Fury-timed all-ins before level 10; you lose if the lane drags out and Dr. Mundo's Adrenaline Rush sustain erases your early damage.

brief.thesis: Renekton holds the lane and solo-kill advantage early because Fury-empowered W (Ruthless Predator) stun-locks Dr. Mundo through burst windows his passive can't out-heal. Adrenaline Rush regenerates a portion of his max health every second, which does nothing against a 10-15 second all-in but fully resets the lane once a skirmish stalls. That tension is exactly why the matchup lands at 44.1% over 338 games despite your early edge: quick stun-chain bursts win, drawn-out trades don't.

theirWindow.what: Burning Agony drains his own health to cut disable duration, and its 1s cooldown means he can use it the instant you land empowered W — expect less than the full 1.5s stun and throw your follow-up damage immediately instead of walking away.

yourWindow.when: Fury over 50, W and E both up
yourWindow.what: Chain empowered W's triple slash (destroys shields, 1.5s stun) into empowered E's Armor shred — this burst spike outruns his per-second Adrenaline Rush regen before he can offset the damage.

powerCurve.note: Adrenaline Rush starts matching your damage
Sadism and HP regen outscale your burst

start.why: Lane sustain and raw damage to keep winning the attrition war against Infected Cleaver poke (42.6% WR, 85.6% pick over 338 games).

boots.why: Mundo is a melee auto-attacker leaning on sustained basic-attack damage between cooldowns; flat damage reduction blunts that chip (43.9% WR, 47.8% pick).

core.why: A burst-heavy two-item spike punishes him before Adrenaline Rush can regenerate back the health you just took.
Stacking Armor shred on top of empowered E's own shred keeps your damage relevant as his HP pool and regen grow.
Converts a chunk of incoming damage into a heal-over-time, directly offsetting his cleaver poke and auto trades (62.5% WR over 24 games in this exact path).

situational.when: he is leaning on healing and regen to win extended trades, per the standard read on this matchup
you need a burst-health buffer to survive his all-in once Sadism comes online
the game goes long and you need sustained DPS to keep pace with his scaling HP pool

runes.keystoneWhy: Stacking adaptive damage and healing across an extended trade is the one thing that can match Adrenaline Rush's per-second regen once a skirmish runs past your burst window.

summoners.why: Ignite's damage-over-time cuts through his healing during your all-in windows, and at 45% win rate with 89.3% pick rate it's the standard answer to a sustain-based laner like Mundo.

playing.title: Track Fury before engaging
playing.detail: Only commit to extended trades at 50+ Fury, where Q, W, and E all get their empowered effects — below that threshold you're trading into his sustain for less reward.

playing.title: All-in between levels 3-5
playing.detail: Your solo-kill advantage is real early; look for kills while Dominus is still on its long early cooldown for both of you and his healing can't outpace a stun-locked burst.

playing.title: Expect a shortened stun
playing.detail: Burning Agony's 1s cooldown lets him shave time off your empowered W's 1.5s stun almost on reaction — land your follow-up damage immediately instead of walking away expecting the full duration.

playing.title: Respect low-HP Mundo
playing.detail: Masochism gives him bonus AD scaling with missing health for several seconds, so a Mundo under half HP hits harder than his bar suggests — don't facecheck him expecting a free kill.

playing.title: Shred Armor on every all-in
playing.detail: Empowered E reduces his Armor on hit — use it first in any engage so your W stuns and autos land for more, since his HP pool only grows over time.

playing.title: Keep trades short
playing.detail: Burning Agony's continual drain and Adrenaline Rush's regen both reward him for staying in a fight — win the exchange in one stun-chain burst rather than skirmishing.

playing.title: Back off once Fury is spent
playing.detail: Once your resources and cooldowns (W 16-8s, E 16-10s by rank) are down, disengage rather than trading evenly — even trades favor his passive regen over time.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the tactical reasoning connecting them to specific ability mechanics and timings is my own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Build up Fury while trying to engage aggressively to gain lane control. Purchase Executioner’s Calling and use it to create a gap in growth by pressuring Dr. Mundo.
